gaps.name: Priority-aware fetch queue with cancel on scroll-away
gaps.whatItIs: FetchManagerImpl keeps one entry per resource with a bag of references, priorities (elevated / user-initiated / visible-index), and cancels a fetch the moment the last reference goes away, so only what is on screen is being pulled and a tapped item jumps the queue.
gaps.whyItMatters: Every call site in our app uses TGClient's plain downloadFile:completion: at default priority, and TGRemoteImageView -cancelLoading only flips a local BOOL - the TDLib download keeps running. Fast-scrolling a chat or the contact list queues dozens of avatar and thumbnail fetches that keep competing with the photo the user actually tapped. On EDGE/3G on a 4S this is the difference between a tap opening in seconds and in a minute.
gaps.whereItGoes: A new small scheduler owned by TGClient (or a TGFetchQueue in src/), called from TGRemoteImageView.m, TGChatViewController.m, TGMediaViewController.m, TGChatListViewController.m; uses the already-wrapped priority argument.
tdlib: downloadFile with priority 1..32 - wrapped as startDownloadingFile:priority:completion:

gaps.name: Per-file transfer status fan-out and in-bubble progress ring
gaps.whatItIs: FileMediaResourceStatus / ChatMessageInteractiveMediaBadge model each media as Remote / Fetching(progress) / Local and draw a per-bubble circular progress with a cancel cross, independently for every visible message.
gaps.whyItMatters: We have one global TGClient.onFileProgress block. TGChatViewController overwrites it for a single downloadingFileId and shows one centred percentage HUD; TGMediaViewController saves and restores the previous block to avoid clobbering it. Only one transfer can be observed at a time, and a bubble downloading in the background shows nothing. Users cannot see or cancel a second download.
gaps.whereItGoes: Replace onFileProgress with a fileId->observers registry in TGClient.m, draw the ring in ChatViewCell.m, delete the HUD in TGChatViewController.m (~line 2308).

gaps.name: Download failure surfacing and tap-to-retry
gaps.whatItIs: Modern clients turn a failed or cancelled fetch back into the Remote state with a download arrow, so a retry is one tap; TDLib reports the failure through updateFile / the request error.
gaps.whyItMatters: Nearly every download callback in our source is `if (path.length == 0) return;` - a failed fetch leaves a spinner or a blank bubble forever with no way to retry short of leaving and re-entering the chat. On a flaky 3G link this is the single most common file-transfer failure a 4S user hits.
gaps.whereItGoes: Same status model as the progress ring: ChatViewCell.m plus the completion blocks in TGChatViewController.m, TGMediaViewController.m, TGProfileViewController.m.
tdlib: getFile / fileInfo: to re-check state - wrapped

gaps.name: Report the real network type to TDLib
gaps.whatItIs: The app watches reachability and calls setNetworkType(wifi/mobile/mobileRoaming/other/none) on every change, which is what makes auto-download limits and the network-usage breakdown mean anything.
gaps.whyItMatters: TGClient+Network.m:460 wraps setNetworkType but nothing in the app ever calls it, and there is no reachability observer anywhere in src/. So TDLib assumes one network forever: our per-network auto-download settings and the Wi-Fi vs mobile columns in the data-usage screen are both fiction, and a user on a metered 3G plan gets Wi-Fi-sized auto-downloads.
gaps.whereItGoes: SCNetworkReachability observer in AppDelegate.m feeding [TGClient setNetworkTypeKind:]; SystemConfiguration is fine on iOS 6.

gaps.name: Keep transfers alive when the app is backgrounded
gaps.whatItIs: A background task assertion held while any download or upload is in flight, so pressing Home mid-send does not freeze the transfer.
gaps.whyItMatters: There is no beginBackgroundTask anywhere in src/. Sending a photo or pulling a video and then locking the phone suspends the process and the transfer stalls until the user returns - on a 4S over 3G a 10MB video is minutes, so this happens constantly. iOS 6 grants ~10 minutes, which is exactly the window this needs.
gaps.whereItGoes: AppDelegate.m applicationDidEnterBackground, driven by the same transfer registry as the progress fan-out.
tdlib: none new; uses the active-transfer set derived from updateFile

gaps.name: Play video and music while they download
gaps.whatItIs: MediaPlayer / UniversalMediaPlayer feed AVPlayer through a resource loader backed by byte-range fetches, so playback starts on the first seconds instead of the whole file.
gaps.whyItMatters: Every video and audio playback path calls the whole-file downloadFile:completion:, so a 20MB video is a multi-minute wait behind a percentage HUD before the first frame. TGClient+Files already exposes the exact primitives a resource loader needs (downloadedPrefixSizeForFile:offset:, downloadFile:offset:limit:, streamFile:offset:count:) and none of them are called from any screen. Only progressive MP4/H.264 is in scope - the 4S cannot decode the modern alternative-quality codecs.
gaps.whereItGoes: An AVAssetResourceLoaderDelegate used by TGMediaViewController.m and the audio player; /Users/alexanderhavrysh/Git/iOS/twelve/Telegraph/TGMusicPlayer.m and TGModernConversationAudioPlayer.m already implement this pattern in Objective-C, so the port is mostly plumbing to streamFile:.

gaps.name: Free-space guard and disk-full handling on download
gaps.whatItIs: Modern clients check available space against the resource size before fetching and surface a clear out-of-space error rather than failing mid-write.
gaps.whyItMatters: TGVideoRecorder.m already does exactly this check for recording (freeDiskSpace / diskFloor), but the download side has no equivalent. A 4S that is nearly full silently fails part-way into a big file, and because failures are not surfaced at all the user just sees a stuck bubble.
gaps.whereItGoes: Same guard helper reused from TGVideoRecorder.m, applied in the fetch scheduler before startDownloadingFile:, with an offer to run the existing storage cleanup in TGStorageViewController.

gaps.name: Cancel an outgoing media send from the bubble
gaps.whatItIs: A pending upload shows its progress on the bubble with a cross that aborts the send and removes the message.
gaps.whyItMatters: We can start uploads (uploadFileAtPath:, cancelUploadOfFile:) but neither is called from any screen, and the sending bubble shows no progress. On a slow uplink a mis-picked 8MB photo is unstoppable and blocks everything queued behind it.
gaps.whereItGoes: ChatViewCell.m sending state plus TGChatViewController.m send path; cancel maps to deleting the pending message, as the header already notes.

gaps.name: Preload the neighbouring photo in the media viewer
gaps.whatItIs: The gallery fetches the next and previous item at low priority while the current one is on screen, so swiping is instant.
gaps.whyItMatters: TGMediaViewController fetches strictly on demand, so every swipe in a photo gallery is a fresh round trip on a link where that is seconds. One low-priority prefetch each side is the cheapest perceived-speed win in the whole file-transfer area, and it is bounded so it costs no memory beyond one extra decoded image.
gaps.whereItGoes: TGMediaViewController.m paging callback, using priority 1 for the neighbours and the tapped item at high priority via the fetch scheduler.
tdlib: downloadFile with priority - wrapped as startDownloadingFile:priority:completion:
